faq.q: How do I make an AI video from a product photo?
faq.a: Upload one clear photo of your item or paste a product page link, choose a video type, frame and length, and run the job. The tool builds the clip around your product and shows the credit cost before you start.

faq.q: How long and wide can an AI video be?
faq.a: You can choose 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds, with 9:16 vertical, 1:1 square and 16:9 wide frames. There are also 3:4 and 4:3 options for listings and pages.
The price shows before each run. A 6-second clip uses 24 credits, 10 seconds uses 40, 15 seconds uses 60 and 30 seconds uses 120. If a job fails, the credits return to your balance automatically.

faq.q: Can I make several versions for A/B testing?
faq.a: Yes. Run the same photo with different actors, openings or scenes, then download each version and split-test them in your ad platform. You do not need another shoot.

faq.q: Can I enter a product page URL instead of a photo?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the link into URL to Video and the tool brings the product image and name into the editor for you to check before making the clip.

faq.q: Do I need to hire a model or creator?
faq.a: No. The people in the clips are generated around your product photo, so there is no casting, sample shipping or filming date. You can still work with a real creator later if you want one.

faq.q: Are these clips suitable for paid social ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube. Add your own captions, prices and offers, and follow each platform's rules for labeling AI content.

faq.q: How long does a video take to make?
faq.a: A finished clip is ready in minutes, and the exact time varies a little with the length and server load. You can start another job while you wait.

overview.h2: What is an AI video generator?
overview.p: An AI video generator makes a clip from a photo, a product link or a short description, without filming, actors on set or a production crew. This one is built for online stores, so every clip is centered on your product.

overview.h2: Types of videos you can generate
overview.p: Creator-style ads explain the product to camera, demos show one feature in use, unboxings reveal the package, and before-and-after clips show a change. You can also add motion to a still photo.

input_guide.h2: Prepare one product photo that can carry the scene

items.d: Use a product shot where the complete shape, main color, and important parts are visible instead of cropping away the feature you want to show.
A little space around the product gives camera movement and hand actions somewhere to happen without cutting into the object.

items.t: Match the photo to the job
items.d: Choose a clean hero shot for motion, a feature view for a demo, and a packaging reference when the box or insert is part of the story.
Name one place, one main action, and one product detail. A single focused moment is easier to judge than a list of unrelated scenes.
Decide on vertical, square, or wide before you describe the composition so the framing fits the place where you will post it.
A quick clip for one short product moment.
Room for a simple action or reveal.
More time to show a product in use.
Room for a complete product story: problem, demo, and result.
A hand pulls a stainless water bottle from a canvas gym bag beside a bench, then turns it toward the light.
A lunch box sits on a kitchen counter while its lid clicks shut and the front latch locks into place.
A matte black mailer opens on a pale table, tissue folds back, and a candle is lifted into view.
A crowded entryway with loose shoes changes to the same space with pairs lined up on a bamboo rack.
Morning light travels across a watch on a stone surface as the camera makes a slow, close push toward the face.
A compact speaker rests on a desk beside a laptop while a hand reaches in to turn the dial.
Add the price, date, discount code, or product name yourself so every character matches the approved source.
Add captions, music, or a spoken track in TikTok, CapCut, Ads Manager, or your usual editor, since the clip does not include them.

items.t: Review from first to last frame
items.d: Look for changes to labels, colors, edges, or small parts before publishing and keep the version that shows the item honestly.
Name files by product, scene, shape, and date so a later test does not overwrite the opening you want to reuse.

good: Small stores testing several product angles from one approved photo

scene_prompt_examples.h2: Turn a broad idea into a clear shot

items.d: Broad: “Show this jar.” More specific: “A hand turns the glass moisturizer jar on a pale vanity; tight framing, soft morning light from the right.” It names one movement, one place, the shot distance and the light, so the jar stays in focus.

Broad: “Show my backpack.” More specific: “A hand pulls the zipper on a navy daypack beside an open train seat; medium close-up, window light across the fabric.” The action and setting tell viewers what to look at.

Broad: “Make a video of my tea.” More specific: “A round tea tin turns on a wooden breakfast table beside a cup; close framing, side light through a kitchen window.” This sets the place and the product details in view.

Broad: “Show how this speaker works.” More specific: “A finger presses the top dial on the speaker at a desk; tight shot, cool daylight from a side window.” One visible gesture gives the scene a clear subject.
